prompts.text: Name a food people eat with their hands
prompts.fact: Pizza's whole design is a handheld wedge, so it edges out burgers and sandwiches.

prompts.text: Name something people spread on their toast
prompts.fact: Butter just beats jam, with peanut butter close enough to steal the top spot.

prompts.text: Name something people dip into a sauce
prompts.fact: Fries win because ketchup is the default dip and fries are the default dipper.

prompts.text: Name something people put in a salad
prompts.fact: Lettuce squeaks past tomato by a hair, since a salad without leaves hardly counts.

prompts.text: Name a vegetable kids refuse to eat
prompts.fact: Broccoli's bitter little trees make it the classic kid standoff, ahead of sprouts.

prompts.text: Name a flavour of crisps or potato chips
prompts.fact: Barbecue scrapes ahead of sour cream and onion, with salt and vinegar right behind.

prompts.text: Name something people put on top of ice cream
prompts.fact: Sprinkles just beat chocolate sauce: the topping that makes a cone look like a party.

prompts.text: Name a kind of nut
prompts.fact: Peanut leads even though it is technically a legume, not a true tree nut.

prompts.text: Name a fruit with a big pit in the middle
prompts.fact: Peaches narrowly beat cherries as the fruit with the stone everyone remembers.

prompts.text: Name a fruit people blend into a smoothie
prompts.fact: Banana is the creamy base of most smoothies, but strawberry is only a whisker behind.

prompts.text: Name a food you might buy at a fair or carnival
prompts.fact: Cotton candy is the fair's signature treat, though popcorn is hot on its heels.

prompts.text: Name a pet other than a dog or a cat
prompts.fact: Fish are the easiest pet to keep, so they just edge out rabbits and hamsters.

prompts.text: Name an animal you'd find on a farm
prompts.fact: Cows, chickens and pigs are nearly tied, since every farm picture includes all three.

prompts.text: Name an animal with spots
prompts.fact: Leopards win the spotted vote, with giraffes and cheetahs close enough to take it.

prompts.text: Name an animal that's known for being slow
prompts.fact: Sloth wins by a whisker, but snails and turtles are just as famous for crawling.

prompts.text: Name an animal people are afraid of
prompts.fact: Snakes and spiders are neck and neck as the animals that scare people most.

prompts.text: Name an animal you might spot in a forest
prompts.fact: Deer edge out squirrels as the creature most expected between the trees.

prompts.text: Name an animal you'd see at a zoo
prompts.fact: Lion, elephant and giraffe are almost tied as the zoo's big three.

prompts.text: Name an insect
prompts.fact: Ants edge out butterflies and bees in a close three-way race for the first bug named.

prompts.text: Name something that has a shell
prompts.fact: Turtles, eggs and snails are almost tied, each the first shell people picture.

prompts.text: Name something people bring to the beach
prompts.fact: A towel is what nearly everyone packs, though sunscreen is close on its heels.

prompts.text: Name a kind of weather that keeps people indoors
prompts.fact: Rain just beats thunderstorms and snow as the weather that cancels the most plans.

prompts.text: Name a colour that flowers come in
prompts.fact: Red just leads, but pink and yellow are nearly as common in any garden.

prompts.text: Name something that's pink
prompts.fact: Pigs squeak ahead of flamingos as the first pink thing people think of.

prompts.text: Name something that's yellow
prompts.fact: Bananas edge out the sun, with lemons close behind in the yellow race.

prompts.text: Name something you see after it rains
prompts.fact: Puddles narrowly beat rainbows: one is guaranteed, the other needs sun.

prompts.text: Name a kind of tree
prompts.fact: Oak just edges pine as the tree people picture first, with palm and maple trailing.

prompts.text: Name something you might see flying in the sky
prompts.fact: Birds edge out airplanes, since birds are the one thing always up there.

prompts.text: Name a famous Chris
prompts.fact: Three Marvel stars named Chris nearly tie, so the top spot is a true coin toss.

prompts.text: Name a famous Jennifer
prompts.fact: Lawrence, Aniston and Lopez are all A-listers, so the votes split three ways.

prompts.text: Name a famous Kevin
prompts.fact: Kevin Hart narrowly edges Bacon and Durant; comedy, film and the NBA collide.

prompts.text: Name a Marvel superhero
prompts.fact: Iron Man launched the MCU in 2008, but Spider-Man and Cap are right on his heels.

prompts.text: Name a superhero's secret identity
prompts.fact: Superman, Spider-Man and Batman: the big three secret identities nearly tie.

prompts.text: Name a famous movie villain
also: The Wicked Witch of the West

Voldemort: He Who Must Not Be Named

prompts.fact: Vader's breath and the Joker's laugh keep these two villains neck and neck.

prompts.text: Name a yellow cartoon character
prompts.fact: SpongeBob and Pikachu are neck and neck; Homer and the Minions trail.

prompts.text: Name a famous cartoon cat
prompts.fact: Garfield's lasagna-loving laziness just edges Tom's endless chases.

prompts.text: Name a Disney princess
prompts.fact: Ariel narrowly tops Cinderella and Belle; Elsa (technically a queen) still ranks fourth.

prompts.text: Name a video game people play online with friends
prompts.fact: Fortnite, Minecraft and Roblox dominate squad-up gaming.

prompts.text: Name a Nintendo character
prompts.fact: Mario is Nintendo's mascot, but Pikachu and Link are never far behind.

prompts.text: Name a starter Pokémon
prompts.fact: Gen 1's fire, water and grass starters are in a three-way dead heat.

We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together
prompts.fact: Shake It Off, Love Story and Blank Space are all signature mega-hits.

prompts.text: Name a place people dream of going on holiday
prompts.fact: Maldives, Bali and Hawaii split the sun-and-sand dream vote almost evenly.

prompts.text: Name a European city you'd love to visit
prompts.fact: Paris wins on romance, but Rome and London are barely behind.

prompts.text: Name a city famous for its skyscrapers
prompts.fact: New York invented the skyline, but Dubai holds the tallest-building record.

prompts.text: Name a winter sport
prompts.fact: Skiing leads, snowboarding follows, and ice skating rounds out the podium.

prompts.text: Name an Olympic sport
prompts.fact: Swimming, gymnastics and athletics are the big three of every Summer Games.

prompts.text: Name a sport played on grass
prompts.fact: Football leads, but cricket, rugby and golf all love a good lawn.

prompts.text: Name a job you dreamed of having as a kid
prompts.fact: Doctor edges teacher and astronaut as the classic childhood career dream.

prompts.text: Name a job where people often work at night
prompts.fact: Nurses keep hospitals running through the night, with security guards close behind.

prompts.text: Name a school subject that students often find hard
prompts.fact: Maths takes the 'hardest' crown, but physics and chemistry are right behind.

prompts.text: Name a school subject students look forward to
prompts.fact: PE wins by a hair, since most students would rather move than sit still.

prompts.text: Name something France is famous for
prompts.fact: The Eiffel Tower has been France's emblem since 1889, with baguettes close behind.

prompts.text: Name something Japan is famous for
prompts.fact: Sushi barely tops anime as Japan's food and pop culture battle for the title.

prompts.text: Name something Switzerland is famous for
prompts.fact: Chocolate squeaks past watches in the land of both.
